source.section: Instructions PDF p.4, RI-1040 lines 1-5; PDF p.5, lines 6-8; PDF p.13, Tax Computation Worksheet ('Use for all filing status types')

worked: Federal AGI = wages 100,000.00 = 100,000.00. Federal taxable income = 100,000.00 - 31,500.00 standard deduction = 68,500.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). RI-1040 line 1 federal AGI 100,000.00. Line 1y total decreasing modifications = 0.00. Line 2a other-state obligations 0.00; line 2m total increasing modifications = 0.00. Schedule M page 2 line 3 net = 0.00 - 0.00 = 0.00; RI-1040 line 2 = 0.00. Line 3 modified federal AGI = 100,000.00 + (0.00) = 100,000.00. Standard Deduction and Exemption Worksheets: line 3 100,000.00 is not more than 254,250.00: the worksheets stop at line 3, full amounts. Line 4 standard deduction: 21,800.00 (Qualifying widow(er)). Line 5 = 100,000.00 - 21,800.00 = 78,200.00. Line 6 exemptions: 1 x 5,100.00 = 5,100.00. Line 7 taxable income = 78,200.00 - 5,100.00 = 73,100.00. Line 8 tax on 73,100.00 by the schedule as numbers: 73,100.00 x 0.0375 = 2741.250000 = 2,741.25. Credits 0.00 (Schedule I, Schedule II, RI earned income credit and RI-1040H are not modelled and not claimed here). Rhode Island income tax = 2,741.25. Note: Qualifying widow(er): 21,800 and one exemption (dependents are not modelled and checks have none).
